title: Quantum encoding of structured light into in-plane topological spin textures
authors: Pavel A. Vorobyev, Daichi Kurebayashi, Oleg A. Tretiakov
abstract: Structured light offers a powerful means of controlling light-matter interactions through multiple tunable optical degrees of freedom. Using micromagnetic simulations, we investigate the nucleation of asymmetric bimerons and antibimerons by pulsed Laguerre-Gaussian optical vortices in chiral ferromagnetic thin films with $C_{nv}$ and $D_{2d}$ symmetries, respectively. For optical vortices with orbital angular momentum (OAM) $|m|=1$, circularly polarized beams deterministically nucleate a single bimeron or antibimeron via the interplay of spin angular momentum, OAM, and magnetic chirality, whereas linearly polarized beams produce textures whose topological charge directly follows the OAM ($Q=m$). Optical vortices with OAM $|m|>1$ nucleate clusters and other configurations composed of multiple spin textures, whose morphology and topological charge depend sensitively on the optical quantum numbers and pulse parameters. These findings reveal a route to topology-selective writing through the encoding of optical quantum numbers into distinct in-plane topological magnetic states.
summary: This research demonstrates how structured light, specifically optical vortices, can be used to write precise, controllable topological spin textures in chiral magnetic films. By controlling the beam's orbital and spin angular momentum, researchers can deterministically encode these quantum optical properties into the magnetic topology, opening a new pathway for quantum-controlled spintronic devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the deterministic and local writing of in-plane topological spin textures (like bimerons and antibimerons) within chiral ferromagnetic thin films using structured light, specifically optical vortices (OVs).
main_result: Structured light provides a versatile route for topology-selective writing, where the optical quantum numbers (OAM, SAM) can be directly encoded into the topological charge (Q) of the resulting magnetic texture.
method: The study employs micromagnetic simulations to model the time evolution of magnetization dynamics driven by pulsed Laguerre-Gaussian optical vortex fields.
model_or_system: The system is an ultrathin ferromagnetic film exhibiting chiral magnetic properties, governed by a free energy functional and simulated using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. The driving force is a time-dependent magnetic field derived from the structured light.
key_observables: Topological charge (Q), magnetic texture morphology (bimerons/antibimerons), and the dependence of these on optical quantum numbers (m, p, polarization s).
important_parameters: Material parameters include $M_s$, $A$, $D$, and $K_x$; simulation parameters involve beam waist ($W$), pulse duration ($t_{	ext{pulse}}$), and OAM ($m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the paraxial approximation for the OV field and assumes the dynamics are governed by the LLG equation under the influence of the structured light pulse.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of OV incidence on a chiral film, the spatial profiles of LG modes, and time-evolution maps showing the nucleation of single or clustered topological textures corresponding to specific input optical parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, detailing the simulation protocol (three-stage writing process), presenting results for specific polarization/OAM combinations, and concluding with a general framework for topology-selective writing.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics (structured light, OAM) directly into condensed matter magnetism, providing a mechanism for non-invasive, quantum-number-controlled manipulation of magnetic topology, which is highly relevant for advanced spintronics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic illustration of the model. An OV beam is incident on a chiral magnetic thin film. The spiral represents the he- lical phase front of the OV, the magenta arrow indicates its propaga- tion direction, and the red arrows denote the initial uniform in-plane magnetization of the chiral magnet. (b) Magnetic configuration of an asymmetric bimeron. (c) Magnetic configuration of an asymmetric antibimeron. The sketches below panels (b) and (c) show the vortex- antivortex pair forming each spin texture.

FIG. 2. Normalized spatial profiles of LG modes at the focal plane (z = 0). The first row, panels (a) to (d), shows the real part Re[Bm,p] of the OV magnetic field. The second row, panels (e) to (h), shows its imaginary part Im[Bm,p]. The third row, panels (i) to (l), shows the corresponding intensity |Bm,p|2. The columns correspond to (m, p) = (0, 0), (1, 0), (2, 0), and (2, 1), respectively. The fields and intensities are normalized to their respective peak values, with the color scales indicated by the colorbars.

FIG. 3. Nucleation outcome diagrams for circularly polarized OVs. The color maps show the topological charge Q as a function of the pulse duration tpulse and the OAM m. Panels (a) and (b) correspond to the Cnv-symmetric system hosting asymmetric bimerons for (a) D > 0 with beam polarization s = 1, and (b) D < 0 with s = −1. Panels (c) and (d) correspond to the D2d-symmetric system hosting asymmetric antibimerons for (c) D > 0 with s = 1, and (d) D < 0 with s = −1.

FIG. 4. Nucleation of single in-plane topological spin textures in a chiral FM driven by circularly polarized OVs. The OV pulse carries OAM index m = 1 and has a total duration of tpulse = 36.5 ps. The top row [panels (a)–(g)] corresponds to right-handed circular polarization (s = −1), leading to the nucleation of an asymmetric bimeron. The bottom row [panels (h)–(n)] corresponds to left-handed circular polarization (s = 1), leading to the nucleation of an asymmetric antibimeron. Panels (a)–(c) and (h)–(j) show the magnetization dynamics during the OV pulse, while panels (d)–(f) and (k)–(m) show the subsequent relaxation after the pulse is switched off, with time reset to t = 0 at the start...

FIG. 5. (a) Nucleation outcome diagram for linearly polarized OVs. The color map shows the topological charge Q as a function of the OV magnetic-field amplitude coefficient B0 and OAM m. (b)–(e) Nucleation of asymmetric bimerons. Panels (b) and (d) show the magnetization states at t = 5 ps during the OV pulse for m = 1 and m = −1 at B0 = 12 T and B0 = 16 T, respectively. The corresponding equilibrium states after relaxation are shown in (c), with Q = 1, and in (e), with Q = −1. The color in panels (b)–(e) represents the out- of-plane magnetization component.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly connects quantum optics (structured light/optical vortices) to the manipulation of magnetic spin textures (topological spin textures) in ferromagnetic films, fitting the theme of quantum-optics concepts applied to spintronics.
